Establishing a homework club at every school is an excellent idea. Ideally, these clubs should meet at least three times a week to provide a space where teachers can help students with their assignments or explain difficult topics. By attending, students can improve their understanding of various subjects, socialize with their peers, and build more confidence in their academic abilities. Whether you need to finish a project, study for an upcoming exam, or simply get your homework done early, these clubs offer a wide range of benefits.

One major advantage of a homework club is the support available for school projects. Working on a big assignment with a friend makes the process more interactive and enjoyable. If a student feels confused about a specific task, they can easily ask a teacher for guidance. Furthermore, as more students join, the club becomes a helpful community where everyone supports each other. Completing a project alone can be quite difficult, but having access to a supportive environment at school ensures that students get the help they need to succeed.

Additionally, homework clubs are the perfect place to prepare for tests and quizzes. Teachers can assist students by creating flashcards, reviewing study guides, or even organizing educational games like Kahoot. These games are a fun way to review material before an exam. Many students find it hard to focus at home because of various distractions, but the club provides a concentrated atmosphere. I highly recommend attending these sessions regularly to ensure you are well-prepared. By using this time effectively, students are much more likely to pass their exams and feel ready for any challenge.

Another benefit is the opportunity to complete homework before even leaving school. This means students do not have to worry about their assignments once they get home. In these clubs, teachers from all subjects—including Math, Science, History, and English—can provide more detailed explanations than they might have time for during a regular lesson. This extra attention helps students learn the material more deeply and ensures they understand the concepts better than they did in class.

In conclusion, a homework club is one of the most valuable programs a school can offer. It helps students gain confidence, improve their grades, and build stronger relationships with their classmates. It creates a positive community of dedicated learners and teachers. To make this a reality, we need students to participate and amazing teachers to volunteer their time. Many people believe that high school students should choose a career path and start working to prepare for their future. However, committing to a specific job at such a young age is not a good idea. It can lead to distractions from academic responsibilities, interrupt the essential learning process, and prevent students from participating in the activities they enjoy.

One major reason to avoid early career commitment is that it interferes with schoolwork. High school becomes more challenging every year, and teachers expect students to take their education seriously. To graduate and get into a good college, students must focus on their homework and prepare for difficult exams. If a student spends too much time working, their grades will likely suffer. For instance, a student working at a hair salon after school might not have enough time to finish their assignments or study for a test. This leads to poor academic performance, which can also hurt a student's self-confidence.

Furthermore, teenagers are still in a stage of development and need to prioritize their education. High school is a time for students to explore different interests and learn the skills necessary for a successful future. By focusing on their studies now, they can eventually earn a higher salary and live a healthy, successful life. If a student commits to a specific job too early, they might miss out on the chance to pursue their true dream career. They need to stay in school and prepare for university rather than being tied down by a job that does not help them grow.

Finally, having a job at a young age can prevent students from doing things they love. Engaging in hobbies and sports is essential for staying healthy and maintaining a positive attitude. When a student has to balance school and a specific career, they often lose the time needed for these enjoyable activities, which can cause a great deal of stress. For example, a student who loves playing football might find that they no longer have time for the team because of their work schedule. Without these positive outlets, students may feel overwhelmed and struggle to find happiness in their daily lives.

In summary, high school students should prioritize their education and personal interests over starting a career. By focusing on their studies and participating in activities they enjoy, they will be better prepared for college and their future dream jobs. Working just to earn money at a young age is not worth the risk to their grades and overall well-being.

In conclusion, inactivity serves a significant purpose because it allows us to finish our work safely and keeps our bodies healthy. Although some believe that constant activity is the key to success, I believe that everyone must decide for themselves when it is time to be idle to maintain their well-being.

Students have enough hours of school already! I strongly disagree about the school board adding more hours to school every day. I am writing to express my strong disagreement with the school board’s proposal to add more hours to the daily schedule. This is not just a personal complaint; this change would negatively impact students, teachers, and the school as a whole.

One major concern is that longer days lead to extreme exhaustion. When students are forced to stay in the same environment for too long, they become restless, which can lead to behavioral issues. Furthermore, academic performance would likely suffer. Tired students cannot focus effectively, and an extended school day leaves them with almost no time at home to complete their homework or study for upcoming tests.

This decision also places a heavy burden on our teachers. Like everyone else, they have families and children who need their time and attention. Staying later at school prevents them from maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Additionally, a longer schedule makes it harder to manage personal responsibilities. For instance, I have monthly orthodontist appointments that currently force me to miss several morning classes. If the school day were not extended, I could potentially move these appointments to the afternoon. As it stands, missing school already results in a mountain of make-up work; adding more hours would only make this situation worse for students who are sick or have medical needs.

From an administrative perspective, the school would face increased costs. There would be a higher demand for food, paper, and bathroom supplies. Even small items, like agendas with bathroom passes, would need to be replaced more frequently. Beyond finances, the school environment might become more hostile. Fatigue often leads to more frequent arguments and physical fights among the student body, and teachers may lose their patience more easily. There are also safety risks to consider. If the school day ends later, our buses will be on the road at the same time as elementary school traffic, significantly increasing the risk of road accidents and congestion.

Ultimately, education is about quality, not just quantity. Students already wake up very early, and adding more time to the day will only lead to burnout. If everyone is exhausted, teachers cannot deliver effective lessons, and students will struggle to retain information. I strongly urge the school board to reconsider this plan and listen to the viewpoints of those who will be most affected. This proposal creates more problems than it solves, and it is important to think about the well-being of the entire school community.

Should teenagers have a curfew? This is a major question for many parents and local governments. Currently, a city council is considering a new curfew law to keep young people safe after dark. The world has changed, and there are more risks than there used to be. This debate raises questions about whether such laws are necessary for protection or if they simply limit a teenager's freedom.

The city council is discussing this policy for several key reasons. Primarily, they want to prevent young people from getting hurt or putting themselves in dangerous situations. Additionally, they aim to protect teenagers from the negative influences found in the world today. Finally, a curfew could stop teens from making poor decisions, such as underage drinking or other illegal activities. By keeping them home at night, the council hopes to reduce trouble in the community.

If this law is passed, would every teenager outside at night be a criminal? The answer depends on the situation. In my view, if a teen is out for a job or because of an emergency, they are not breaking the law. Similarly, if they are accompanied by an adult, they should be allowed to be out because they are supervised. However, if they are just wandering around with friends or going to parties, then they would be violating the curfew. The legality of being out late should be based on the purpose of the activity.

There is also the question of whether these rules are helpful or just annoying. Most teenagers would argue that a curfew interferes with their social lives and their desire to have fun. However, these laws are designed to ensure their safety. Many young people try to leave their homes at night without their parents' permission, which is very risky. Even if a teenager thinks they are safe, things can go wrong quickly. It is important for them to consider if the risk of being out late is truly worth it.

In conclusion, the debate over teen curfews involves many different perspectives. While the city council wants to prevent accidents and bad behavior, many young people feel their freedom is being restricted. Ultimately, the law would likely include exceptions for work or family time, while targeting unsupervised social gatherings. While teens might see it as an interference, the main goal is to keep them safe from harm.

AVID is a wonderful educational program for any student who has a dream they want to reach. There are several reasons why this activity is so beneficial. First, it helps you grow as an individual while encouraging you to pursue a college education. Second, the program provides tutorials that help you track your progress and improve in all your subjects. Additionally, students get the chance to go on exciting field trips. Finally, being in AVID feels like having a second family that supports you no matter where you go.

In AVID, you learn how to be a responsible and diligent student. For example, weekly binder checks teach you how to stay organized. It is more than just a regular class; it is a place where everyone shares a common goal. We understand that we must keep working hard and never quit until we reach our objectives. While not every teenager thinks about college, those of us who do must be careful about who we spend time with. Being around the wrong crowd can pull you down like the weight of the ocean and make it hard to get back to where you used to be. You can still be friendly with different types of people, but from my perspective, it is important not to get caught up in negative behaviors that might ruin your future.

Tutorials are another essential part of the program. They allow you to show your teachers and classmates how much effort you are putting into your studies. During these sessions, you stand in front of a small group to explain a specific problem you are struggling with. This process helps you gain confidence and allows you to learn from your peers by sharing ideas. Tutorials also reveal your personality. Even if you are naturally shy and prefer to listen rather than speak, participating in these groups helps you step out of your comfort zone and engage with others.

Furthermore, AVID offers unique field trip opportunities that many other students do not have. You can visit various college campuses to see what they are like and meet new people. These trips are both educational and fun because you get to explore the campus with a guide. One of the most exciting parts of the program is participating in fundraisers to earn trips to places like King's Dominion. These rewards are important because they celebrate your hard work. When you are pushing yourself every day to succeed, having something fun to look forward to keeps you motivated. Just as I am motivated by my niece to do my best, AVID provides the support and encouragement needed to stay strong through difficult tasks like taking Cornell notes.

For many students, AVID is truly a family. We all support each other, and there is a culture of kindness where no one speaks badly about anyone else. Even though we come from many different backgrounds and places around the world, we stand together. If a student feels like giving up, the rest of the group ensures they stay on track. We live by the motto "dream, believe, achieve." This program doesn't just help with schoolwork; it makes you, your parents, and your family proud of your progress.

In conclusion, AVID is an enjoyable activity because it allows you to meet new people and build lasting friendships. It offers great programs and activities that help you grow. Most importantly, it provides a supportive environment where you can truly be yourself without having to pretend. Joining AVID is a chance worth taking because it can lead you in a positive direction and help you become a successful person in life.

Many people believe that a positive mindset is the secret to a successful life, but in reality, a hardworking attitude is the true key to achievement. Simply being optimistic does not guarantee that you will reach your objectives, earn a high school diploma, or secure a good job after university. To truly succeed, you must be willing to study hard, work long hours, and step out of your comfort zone.

Achieving your goals requires diligence rather than just hope. For example, if your goal is to buy a new car next year, a positive attitude alone will not cover the costs. You have to consider the practical requirements, such as monthly insurance payments and the price of the vehicle itself. This means you will likely have to work more, and your available income will decrease because of these new expenses. Ultimately, you cannot get a car just by thinking positively; you need a hardworking attitude to actually earn it.

Some might argue that a positive attitude helps you graduate from high school, but this is not realistic. Completing your education is a task that takes twelve years of constant effort. It is impossible to stay positive every single day for over a decade. There are many days when you might be sick or exhausted and just want to go home, yet you have to find a way to survive until the end of the school day. Success in school is about pushing through those difficult moments when you feel like giving up, not just maintaining a cheerful mood.

The path through university is even more demanding. Students often spend years studying difficult subjects just to secure a better future for themselves and their families. This journey involves sleepless nights, endless essays, and the stress of trying to pay for the next semester. After graduating, the challenge continues as you must compete with many other candidates for a job and start paying back bank loans. In a job interview, you have to prove that you are the best person for the position through your experience and dedication, which comes from years of labor, not just a smile.

In conclusion, a successful life is built on reaching major milestones like graduating and finding a stable career. Not everyone has the opportunity to attend school or university, and many people spend their lives working hard while hoping for a miracle or a lottery win to change their lives. Relying on a positive attitude will not take you anywhere. Only a dedicated, hardworking approach can truly help you reach your goals in the real world.

Who doesn't want to be left in the house all day using an electronic device with online access? Although students save money and time by taking classes from home. It is not beneficial to learn online because students lose focus of what they are learning and tend to easily get distracted when they're in their house, students can't have a one on one conversation with a teacher nor discuss with classmates, and students could also face technical difficulties when attending online classes from home.

Losing focus has a big impact in learning. For example, my friend Generic_Name sent me a text message last month, right when I started studying for my history mid-term exam. I responded back to Generic_Name's text, and without realizing we kept on messaging past midnight. This shows how easily students get distracted at home with a cellular device and how easy it is to lose focus. The next morning I decided to get to school an hour early and review one on one with my teacher.

Secondly, taking classes online doesn't just mean you don't have a physical teacher or instructor that you can question lively, but also means that it will be challenging to find answers to your questions. I remember in my sophomore year a kid in our econ class named Generic_Name was really sick for a while so he had ended up taking classes online. Generic_Name was a straight A student, always was first to answer the teachers questions and he also used to ask questions. Thankfully Generic_Name healed towards the end of the year and I asked him if he benefited and if he recommends attending classes from home. The straight A student Generic_Name said it was a real challenge to take the class online and he finished the class a month after he should have with a B- average. Generic_Name had also said that one of the most difficult parts about attending a class online was his laptop not functioning at all times, and not having a teacher you can talk and converse with one on one.

Finally, using your personal computer and internet connection can always be an issue. You can't always depend on your computer, not just the computers but even people aren't perfect. Another main problem Generic_Name had when attending classes online was his laptop and network connection. Generic_Name explained that he always faced technical difficulties. When his laptop wasn't functioning right, the only thing he could do was to stop the lesson and wait for his dad to get the laptop repaired, which took time. Each month, either his laptop or internet connection would not cooperate, so he finished the class a month later than everyone.

In conclusion, Everyone would like to save money and time by taking classes from home. But getting distracted, not asking your teacher questions when you need to, and wasting money on laptop repair is not worth it at all. Learning from a far distance could also be an option but when asking if it is beneficial, we can say that it is not by looking at the listed reasoning.

I recall a classmate who was an excellent student but had to switch to online learning for a while due to health issues. Although he was usually the first to participate in class, he struggled significantly with the remote format. After he returned, he explained that his grades had dropped because he could not have real-time discussions with the teacher. He found it much more difficult to understand the material without that personal interaction.

Finally, depending on personal hardware and internet connections can be a major disadvantage. Technology is not always reliable, and equipment failure can interrupt learning. My classmate experienced this firsthand when his laptop and network connection frequently failed. Whenever his computer broke, he had to stop his lessons and wait for repairs, which wasted a lot of time. Due to these recurring technical issues, he ended up finishing the course an entire month later than the rest of the students.

In conclusion, while the convenience of learning from home is tempting, the drawbacks are serious. The tendency to get distracted, the lack of personal support from instructors, and the stress of technical failures make online classes less effective. When considering whether this method is beneficial, the evidence suggests that traditional classroom learning is a much better option.

Asking for several opinions is a great way to make smarter decisions. By listening to different people, we can gain new perspectives, discover more choices, and find better ways to solve problems. In fact, relying on only one person's advice can sometimes lead to negative consequences.

First, hearing different viewpoints helps us find the right path. For instance, imagine a girl named Maria looking for a specific store at a large mall. She first asked a man for directions, and he told her it was on the second floor. However, after searching there and finding nothing, she decided to ask someone else. This second person explained that the store was actually on the first floor next to an ice cream shop. Because Maria sought a second opinion, she successfully found the store and even enjoyed an ice cream. If she had only listened to the first person, she would have remained lost and frustrated.

Secondly, having more than one source of information is often more reliable. Consider a student who just moved to New York and was nervous about her first day of high school. She and her parents were unsure of the exact location of her classroom. At first, she followed another student she assumed was going to the same place, but she quickly realized she was in the wrong area. Instead of giving up, she began asking several people in the hallway for directions. By gathering multiple answers that all pointed to the same location, she felt confident she was finally going the right way. If she had relied on just one person, she might have ended up in the wrong room again.

Furthermore, seeking multiple opinions can help solve dangerous problems. For example, a teenager was cooking with friends when a small fire started in the oven. Panicked, she asked her friends what to do. One friend suggested throwing water on it, while the other insisted on calling emergency services immediately. By considering both options, she realized that calling 911 was the safest and smartest choice. The firefighters arrived and handled the situation, preventing her house from burning down. Having different suggestions allowed her to pick the best solution during a crisis.

In conclusion, looking for multiple opinions helps individuals make better choices by providing different perspectives and more solutions to problems. Whether it is finding a store in a mall, navigating a new school, or handling an emergency, gathering more information leads to better results. As shown in these examples, things could have ended poorly if only one opinion had been considered.

They say the you should never judge a book by its cover and, especially regarding people, its true. In this case, the cover is not necessary meaning the appearance, but the first impression of another person. Like the cover of a book, first impressions are not always as appealing as what is really there. its not until after you start "reading" or get to know someone, when you really find out that what you see is not always what you get. There are several factors that can affect the first impression that one receives from another. Differing personality, situations and representation of a person, make impressions often the worst means of judging people.

A person's personality has a big effect on the first impressions that they emit. Everybody is different but when it comes down to it first impressions are really based off of whether you are shy or not. I met my best friend after moving during my junior year, at my new high school. Before i knew her, she never said a word to me or anyone else in the classes that she was kind of odd, but then realized that I was the same way, i didn't talk to many people either because of my personality. I knew that I was shy person and after I get to know someone, I put down my front and show my true colors. I thought that maybe she would be same way. After starting to talk to her a little more each day, our friendship grew and I learned that she wasn't odd at all, but just like me an outgoing person hidden by their shyness. Some people like me and my friend, are shy and put up a reserved and quiet front when facing new people. Based on my first impressions of my friend, I thought something that was far from the truth. One who has a shy personality might in reality be outgoing, but uncomfortable showing it at first, making the first impression of that person a mistaken one.

Your first impression of someone is not suitable because you do not know the situation they may be in. When seeing or meeting someone new, you have no idea the kind of day,

difficulties or kind of disappointment that person may be experiencing. They may have have recently lost someone, or could be someone new and yet still have to deal with the routines and stresses going through out their day. All of these situations can create a barrier between themselves and others, and setting of a good impression is probably not at the top of their list of important things to do.

On my first day of senior year, I walked hurriedly to my first class, even thought I had plenty of time to get there. When I walked into my class, the only thing on my mind was to find a seat right away, no matter if it was by another person or not. when the time come to eat lunch, I sat by myself and ate it quickly so I could proceed to my next class. I was so worried about being late for a class, finding a seat and just doing things right, that i didn't have time to try to leave any good first impression, on any of my peers. It wasnt even on my mind to do so. My peers received the impression that i was nervous and not a sociable person, when really I was acting the way I was because of the situation that I was in.

There are many factors that lead to someone's first impression of another. Someone;s personality, current situation, or the way they happen to present themselves all influences the way someone thinks about another when seeing or meeting them for the first time. Since what they think is based off of these judgments, their first impressions is usually wrong. If all friendships were based on first impressions, there would be a lot less of them in the world. First impressions are more often worst means of judging a person because its not until you get to really know a person, you are better equipped to understand what kind person they truly are, and really know the individual based on real values, rather than their first impression or "book cover".

I met my best friend after moving during my junior year at my new high school. Before i knew her, she never said a word to me or anyone else in the classes. I thought that she was kind of odd, but then I realized that I was the same way. I didn't talk to many people either because of my personality. I knew that I was shy person and after I get to know someone, I put down my front and show my true colors. I thought that maybe she would be same way. After starting to talk to her a little more each day, our friendship grew and I learned that she wasn't odd at all, but just like me an outgoing person hidden by their shyness. Some people like me and my friend are shy and put up a reserved and quiet front when facing new people. Based on my first impressions of my friend, I thought something that was far from the truth. One who has a shy personality might in reality be outgoing but uncomfortable showing it at first, making the first impression of that person a mistaken one.

Your first impression of someone is not suitable because you do not know the situation they may be in. When seeing or meeting someone new, you have no idea the kind of day, difficulties or kind of disappointment that person may be experiencing. They may have recently lost someone, or could be someone new and yet still have to deal with the routines and stresses going through out their day. All of these situations can create a barrier between themselves and others. Setting of a good impression is probably not at the top of their list of important things to do.

On my first day of senior year, I walked hurriedly to my first class, even thought I had plenty of time to get there. When I walked into my class, the only thing on my mind was to find a seat right away, no matter if it was by another person or not. When the time come to eat lunch, I sat by myself and ate it quickly so I could proceed to my next class. I was so worried about being late for a class, finding a seat and just doing things right, that i didn't have time to try to leave any good first impression on any of my peers. It wasnt even on my mind to do so. My peers received the impression that i was nervous and not a sociable person, when really I was acting the way I was because of the situation that I was in.

There are many factors that lead to someone's first impression of another. Someone;s personality, current situation, or the way they happen to present themselves all influences the way someone thinks about another when seeing or meeting them for the first time. Since what they think is based off of these judgments, their first impressions is usually wrong. If all friendships were based on first impressions, there would be a lot less of them in the world. First impressions are more often worst means of judging a person. It is not until you get to really know a person that you are better equipped to understand what kind person they truly are and really know the individual based on real values, rather than their first impression or "book cover".

People often say that you should never judge a book by its cover, and this is particularly true when it comes to meeting new people. In this context, the "cover" represents the first impression someone makes. Just like a book's exterior, an initial meeting does not always reflect the quality of what is inside. It is only after you "read" the person by getting to know them that you discover their true character. Several factors, such as different personalities and specific life situations, mean that first impressions are often the least accurate way to evaluate others.

A person’s natural personality has a major impact on the image they project. Frequently, first impressions are simply a reflection of whether a person is shy or confident. For instance, I met my best friend after transferring to a new high school during my junior year. Before we became close, she never spoke to anyone in our classes, which made me think she was a bit strange. However, I soon realized that I was behaving in the exact same way. Because of my own shy personality, I tend to be very quiet until I feel comfortable enough to show my true self. I hoped she might be the same, and as we began talking more each day, our friendship grew. I eventually learned that she was actually a very social and outgoing person who was simply hiding behind her shyness. My first impression was far from the truth, proving that a reserved exterior can often hide a very different reality.

Furthermore, first impressions are often inaccurate because we do not know the specific circumstances a person is facing. When we meet someone for the first time, we have no idea if they are having a difficult day or dealing with a personal disappointment. They might be grieving a loss or simply struggling with the stress of a busy schedule. In these moments, projecting a friendly image is usually not their main priority. These external pressures create a barrier, making it difficult for their real personality to shine through.

I remember experiencing this myself on the first day of my senior year. I was rushing to my first class, even though I had plenty of time. My only focus was finding a seat and making sure I was prepared. When lunch arrived, I sat alone and ate quickly so I could get to my next classroom. I was so worried about following the rules and being on time that I didn't even think about being social or making a good impression on my peers. Consequently, my classmates thought I was an anxious and unsociable person. In reality, I was just overwhelmed by the situation I was in, and their impression of me was completely wrong.

In conclusion, many factors influence how we perceive others during a first meeting. A person’s personality, their current stress levels, and the way they handle specific situations all shape our initial thoughts. Because these judgments are based on limited information, they are frequently incorrect. If all relationships were based only on first impressions, there would be far fewer friendships in the world. We are only able to truly understand someone once we look past the "cover" and learn about their real values and character over time.

Most students eagerly anticipate their summer holidays as a time to relax and enjoy themselves. While some people suggest shortening the summer to have longer breaks in the winter or spring, I believe the traditional long summer vacation is better. My main reasons are that it allows students to make significant long-term plans and that frequent breaks can disrupt the learning process.

Firstly, a lengthy summer break is essential for students who want to organize major activities. For instance, many students wish to travel abroad or visit family members who live in other countries. If the vacation is too short, they might spend their entire trip worrying about upcoming school assignments. Furthermore, international travel takes time; a brief break does not allow enough time to truly experience a new culture or spend quality time with relatives they might not see for many years. Having a long period of free time ensures that these experiences are meaningful rather than rushed.

Secondly, having short periods of school followed by frequent breaks is not an effective way to learn. This can be compared to sports or music. Athletes stay focused during their season to maintain their physical rhythm, and musicians must practice every day to improve. If a student studies for only a few weeks and then takes a break, they lose their academic momentum. It is much more efficient to stay in a "school rhythm" for a longer period and then have a substantial rest, rather than constantly stopping and starting.

Some might argue that shorter, more frequent breaks help students who prefer to study intensely for a short time. However, this approach often leads to "cramming," where students memorize a lot of information quickly and then forget it during the break. While they might get good grades temporarily, they often have to relearn the material later. Therefore, a long summer break after a complete academic year is a more logical structure for retaining knowledge.

In conclusion, summer vacation is often the highlight of the year for students. Although some suggest redistributing holiday time throughout the year, this could ruin many students' summer plans and decrease their learning efficiency. A longer break provides a wider range of opportunities and allows for a more balanced lifestyle. Ultimately, while it depends on how each person uses their time, a long summer vacation offers the best chance for personal growth and relaxation.

For the most part, individuals have the power to regulate how they feel and react. However, there are moments when emotions become difficult to manage and may briefly spiral out of control.

While we try to stay in charge, some traits or feelings seem to happen automatically. For instance, intense emotions like anger, sadness, or depression can be hard to restrain. When these feelings take over, they can lead to dangerous or regrettable behavior because the person is no longer in command of themselves. This is why character traits are sometimes seen as either positive or negative depending on the situation.

People hold different opinions on this matter. Those who believe we choose our traits argue that they feel in control of their reactions and can decide how to behave. Conversely, others feel that their character is not within their power, claiming that emotions simply arise during daily activities like work. This often happens with negative feelings, which can feel overwhelming and impossible to stop.

In conclusion, whether character is a choice or an influence depends largely on the individual. Even those who struggle with their emotions can learn to stay in control by practicing simple techniques. Ultimately, there is a significant difference between actively shaping your own character and letting outside influences dictate who you are.

To what degree should schools limit a student's extracurricular involvement? While schools play a role, the final decision should mostly rest with the family. Educational institutions should only intervene if a student's academic performance suffers, if parents request a change, or if the student's attendance at these activities is inconsistent.

Primarily, the choice to enroll in clubs or sports should belong to the student and their parents. Families understand the student's schedule best and can see if there is enough time for studying and homework. If parents feel their child is overwhelmed, they should discuss the issue with them. If they decide to withdraw the student from an activity, they simply need to inform the school counselor and the person in charge of the program.

On the other hand, schools must step in if a student's grades begin to decline. In this situation, a guidance counselor should meet with the student to identify the cause. If having too many activities is the problem, the student should be required to drop some until their academic performance improves. This approach teaches students that participating in extracurriculars is a privilege that requires maintaining good grades.

Furthermore, attendance is a key factor. If a student frequently misses meetings without a good reason—perhaps more than five times a month—they should face consequences. The school should notify the parents and potentially remove the student from the group or suspend them for a period. This ensures that students remain committed to the activities they choose.

In summary, schools should have limited authority over a student's outside activities. The family should be the main decision-maker. However, the school has a responsibility to intervene if the student fails their classes or fails to show up for their scheduled meetings.

While year-round schools offer more frequent breaks throughout the year, they significantly reduce the length of summer vacation. This schedule creates several problems, including increased stress for everyone involved, limited time for travel, and financial disadvantages for both students and the government.

One major concern is the added stress. For students, attending school almost all year means they constantly worry about their appearance and what clothes to wear. This often leads to buying more clothing just to avoid repeating outfits and to look better than their peers. Teachers also face pressure because they have to continuously plan lessons and grade assignments without a long period to rest and recover.

Another issue is the lack of vacation time in the summer. With only three or four weeks off, students do not have enough time to travel abroad for an extended period. This also affects parents, as responsible parents cannot easily go on long trips if their children are still in school. A short break simply does not provide the same freedom as a traditional three-month summer.

Furthermore, year-round schooling results in less money being earned. Students who usually work during the summer cannot make much money in just one month compared to a full three-month break. Additionally, the government faces higher costs because they must pay for electricity, water, and maintenance for the school buildings throughout the entire year.

Although some people argue that frequent breaks help students remember what they have learned, the reality is that constant studying without a long rest leads to burnout. Even though there are more breaks during the year, they do not make up for the loss of a proper summer vacation.

If I had to choose a subject to teach elementary school students, I would select science. While some might suggest math because of its focus on numbers, I believe science is the best choice because it is part of our lives every time we flip a light switch or toss a ball into the air. One major reason to teach science is that it is incredibly fun for both teachers and students. The subject allows for various hands-on experiments that keep everyone engaged. For instance, when learning about kinetic and potential energy, students can actually throw balls to see these concepts in action. Furthermore, science is a social experience. When a student performs an experiment, the whole class can watch and learn together. Activities like an "egg drop" challenge encourage students to talk to one another, share their observations, and learn from their successes or failures. Ultimately, the excitement of conducting experiments makes science a favorite for many.

Additionally, science is one of the simplest subjects to teach to young children. Unlike English, which requires memorizing many root words, or math, which relies on complex formulas, science mostly requires understanding basic terminology and paying attention to what happens during a demonstration. Instead of practicing the same math problems repeatedly, students can learn by simply observing. It is also a very visual subject. If a student struggles to understand a concept through words, a teacher can easily draw a picture or a diagram to illustrate the point. This combination of drawing and doing makes science much more accessible than subjects that rely strictly on rote memorization.

Finally, science is the most practical subject because it is used constantly in daily life. Almost everything we encounter relates to scientific principles. For example, science explains how light works or how air conditioning moves currents of air through a room. It also helps us understand tools we use, such as how a compass reacts to the Earth's magnetic field. By teaching science, we help students understand how to fix things and how technology works, such as the way an electrical circuit allows a light to turn on instantly. It provides the answers to how the world functions, making it a vital tool for any young person.

In summary, science is the perfect lesson for elementary schoolers because it brings joy to the classroom, is easy to explain through visuals, and has endless real-world applications. It is a subject that makes students smile while they gain valuable knowledge. I look forward to preparing a science lesson soon, as it is clearly the most rewarding way to help children learn about the world.

The impact of technology on our daily lives is a topic that is frequently debated. In my opinion, technology has a very positive influence because so much of our world is now accessible online. From reading digital books to staying in touch through laptops and smartphones, technology makes life more convenient. While some people have a negative view because of what they see on the news, I believe the advantages are clear.

For example, during a long road trip, you can easily read on a smartphone or tablet to stay entertained. This is especially helpful for busy parents who want to relax while their children are sleeping. Digital books are also very portable and impossible to lose. Furthermore, they offer useful features like automatic bookmarks, instant definitions, and translation tools for words you do not understand.

Technology also makes it much easier to stay connected with people who live in other states or countries. Instead of sending a letter and waiting many days for a response, we can use tablets or laptops for video calls. This allows for face-to-face interaction regardless of the distance. Additionally, email is an efficient way to share drafts of your work and get feedback from others. Video conferencing also allows groups of people to meet whenever they are free, which is much more flexible than trying to meet in person when everyone has a busy schedule.

As technology continues to advance, it is becoming a central part of education. Even young children use tablets to learn their ABCs and basic math. Many schools now provide laptops to ensure students have the necessary tools for their assignments. Students enjoy using technology because they can research topics for their projects or watch educational videos that explain difficult concepts. While these devices can be expensive and must be handled with care, they are becoming essential for learning. In the future, we might eventually stop using paper and pencils altogether as everything moves to digital formats.

In conclusion, technology provides us with many efficient ways to communicate and learn. It is becoming a huge part of our lives, and it is important for everyone to get used to these changes. Although some people might miss traditional paper, digital tools are a faster and more reliable way to stay connected. As technology continues to grow, it will only become more important in our daily routines.

I strongly disagree with Emerson’s perspective that extreme individuality is a positive trait, and I have several reasons for this stance. I am lucky to have many important people in my life, including my parents, my sister, and close friends who are like family. Having these connections is essential because they make navigating life much easier. If we were to reject these relationships in favor of total independence, we would likely end up living a very lonely life in deep solitude. We must have faith in one another to get through difficult times.

I experienced this firsthand when I was between twelve and fourteen years old. At that time, I struggled with my grades and felt a constant sense of anxiety about going to school. I didn't think I had the motivation to improve my academic performance or my social skills. Because I was only focused on myself, I often felt depressed and miserable. Everything changed when I finally realized that I needed the support of others. As I spent more time with the people around me, I began to improve naturally. Living a life shared with others allows you to change for the better, often without even noticing it, which proves that anyone is capable of growth if they have the right support.

Furthermore, a life without social connection can be incredibly boring. When you are always alone, you miss out on the joy of conversation and companionship. Having a circle of friends makes life much more entertaining and meaningful. Through shared experiences like playing games, traveling, and socializing, we learn important life lessons and create lasting memories. Some people claim that we live in a society where no one cares about anyone else, but that is not true. While it is true that some people can be negative and push others away, this usually happens because they are afraid or feel ignored. The solution is to stay open to others and ask for help when it is needed.

In conclusion, focusing too much on individuality can lead to a negative and isolated path. Having other people in our lives is a necessity because we can lift each other up, and no one is truly worthless. Leaving someone to struggle on their own is tragic, whereas helping others makes us better people and leads to a more fulfilling life. You should never let others dictate who you are, but you should also recognize that being alone is not the answer. You are the protagonist of your own life, but your story is much better when it is shared with others.

Have you ever considered how much easier it would be to attend classes from the comfort of your own home? Although some critics argue that remote education is not beneficial, I believe it offers important advantages. Specifically, distance learning can be a great help to students with physical disabilities and can provide a fresh perspective for those who struggle in a traditional school setting.

Those who disagree with online learning often have their reasons. They worry that students might face difficulties with social interaction later in life or become overly dependent on digital devices. For example, I have a friend who prefers being online so much that he spends his time playing video games rather than interacting with his family or friends. While these are valid concerns, they do not apply to every student.

Distance learning is particularly helpful for students with disabilities. When I lived in Honduras, I had a friend who used a wheelchair. It was very difficult for her to get to school every day. Her mother had to push her for thirty minutes just to reach the building, and once there, my friend had to struggle to move between the classrooms, the restroom, and the playground. Because of this long and tiring journey, she was often late and too exhausted to focus on her lessons. If she had been able to study from home, she would have saved time and energy, allowing her to get enough sleep and pay better attention to her teachers.

Additionally, online classes can help students see education in a new way. Last year, my cousin was failing his classes and felt like he was not meant for school. He hated the early mornings and the overall environment. After talking to a school counselor, he decided to try distance learning. This change was amazing for him; his grades improved significantly, and he finally felt successful. My cousin was not a bad student; he simply needed a different educational approach. Distance learning allowed him to experience school in a way that suited his specific needs.

In conclusion, distance learning is a vital option that supports students with various challenges. It ensures that students with disabilities have their needs met and gives those who struggle in traditional classrooms a chance to excel. By providing different ways to learn, we can help all students feel equal and capable of reaching their goals, regardless of their circumstances.

Humanity has survived for so long because we learned the importance of staying united and sharing responsibilities. This history teaches us that "two heads are better than one" and that many tasks are simply too difficult to complete alone. From building complex architecture to creating fast ways to cross the ocean, our greatest achievements are the result of collective effort. It is hard to imagine a single person accomplishing these feats, which is why teamwork is so essential.

When you become part of a team, it is usually because you possess a specific skill that benefits the group. For example, if you work at a company that develops websites, you might contribute your expertise in coding or graphic design. In this sense, you are like a specialized part in a large machine. When every part fits perfectly and functions at a steady pace, the entire system runs smoothly without putting unnecessary pressure on any individual member.

Furthermore, working in a team allows the workload to be divided fairly. In a construction crew, workers distribute materials like cement in specific portions to ensure efficiency and avoid waste. Similarly, a good team assigns tasks according to what each person can manage, preventing anyone from becoming overworked. We see this in a professional kitchen as well: while one person peels vegetables, another prepares a mix, and a third adds the finishing touches. Each person has a clear role to play.

In conclusion, teamwork provides numerous benefits for everyone involved. Much like a well-oiled machine, successful collaboration relies on effective communication. When everyone understands their specific duties, the group can function as a single, efficient unit. Teamwork is perhaps the most important lesson we can learn because there will always be goals that we cannot reach on our own.

The statement is "the first impression is almost impossible to change" which is a different feeling for everybody, but for me, I disagree. In fact, the first impression is really important and sometimes true, but I think the first impression does not define a person, an object or a situation. Having a first impression is a human reflex, like having an opinion or a judgment. We are doing it unconsciously.

The first impression is most of the time not real, you need to search deeper to make an opinion and when you really have an opinion, then, the first impression is not important anymore. For example, when you meet someone, your first impression might be that you think she is supercilious and even a little bit mean. Therefore when you really get to know her deeper then you will find that she just had a bad day and that she is nice and sociable. Sometimes it's the contrary, a person seems really nice but in reality she is not, so your first impression was wrong. It is not good to stay on a first impression because most of the time it's wrong.

Moreover, the physic, behaviors or attitude can change an impression. If the person do not smile and seems to be rude but in reality is the nicest person, then it will be awkward for you because you thought she was bad. Sometimes a person can have a bad reputation because of the first impression he shows and it is not his fault, some persons just don't smile every time. Sometimes you can be disappointed because you didn't get to know the person because of your first impression.

The first impressions is not only for people but also for a situation or an object. For example if you are in a library and you want to buy a book, the first thing you are going to do is looking at the cover of the book. If it's pretty you will more easily choose this one instead of a book with a black cover and only the title, because it is your first impression. But your first impression is wrong because you didn't take time to read the resume and you will find soon that the pretty book is actually boring instead of the black book which is really interesting. An object can look nice but have a bad quality. The first impression is the color and the shape of the object, like the physic and the attitude of a person.

In conclusion I would say that the first impression is sometimes right but most of the time it's not. In my opinion, you must not keep in mind your first impression of a person, it's most of the time wrong. You have to get to know the person to build your own opinion. It is normal to have a first impression, like judging, but you must not take the habit to stick with your first impression.

The city council is currently debating whether to implement a curfew for teenagers, which would be set at 10 p.m. on school nights and midnight on weekends. Under this proposal, being out past these hours would be a violation of the law. Although people do not always agree with every regulation, we have a responsibility to follow them. Parents should carefully consider the risks their children face when they are out late. There are many dangerous situations that can arise, and in today’s world, anything can happen. Without the supervision of an adult, minors are more vulnerable to being harmed. A curfew is a practical tool to prevent these incidents from occurring. While teenagers often want more freedom to spend time with their friends—and I remember feeling the same way and sometimes even ignoring my own mother’s rules—it is our responsibility to teach them right from wrong. Eventually, most young people realize that these rules exist because their parents are deeply concerned about their well-being.

To illustrate these risks, consider the tragic story of a young man in New York. He was a wonderful child who was very close to his family and focused on his education. He was not the type of person to get into trouble and usually stayed home. However, one night after dark, he was attacked by a group of individuals outside a small food market just a few blocks from his house. Even though he tried to find help and reach a hospital, he unfortunately passed away on the sidewalk. His attackers later admitted that they had mistaken him for someone else. This innocent boy lost his life through no fault of his own. If he had waited until the next day to go out or if he had been accompanied by a parent, the situation might have ended differently. This shows that being out alone at night is simply not as safe as being at home or with a guardian.

Some people might argue that they want to give their children the freedom they lacked when they were young. They may believe that a curfew is unnecessary if they trust their child. However, the issue is not a lack of trust in the teenager, but rather a lack of trust in the other people who are out at night. It is possible to enjoy life and have fun during daylight hours when it is much safer. During the day, there are many people around who can help if you are in danger. At night, most people are asleep, and the streets are empty, making it much harder to find assistance if something goes wrong.

In conclusion, the city council should consider the current state of the world and do what is best for teenagers by establishing a curfew. Young people can still enjoy their lives and have freedom while following these rules. Implementing a curfew would keep minors safe and help them stay out of trouble, which is a goal that almost everyone can support.

He did not seem to enjoy explaining lessons more than once, which made me so uncomfortable that I asked my counselor to change my schedule. If you meet someone during a difficult moment, they might seem unfriendly, but this does not mean they are a mean person. To truly understand someone, you have to look beyond a single negative interaction and consider the circumstances they might be facing.

For instance, someone might appear very polite and friendly at first but eventually prove to be dishonest. Conversely, a person who seems unapproachable might actually be a very caring individual who will support you in the future. Relying only on initial appearances can lead to wrong conclusions.

In conclusion, first impressions are definitely capable of changing. They are often influenced by temporary bad moods or misleading outward appearances. It is vital to learn about a person’s real character before making a final judgment. By being patient and open-minded, you may discover that the person you initially misjudged is exactly the person you need in your life.

I strongly believe that maintaining a positive attitude is the essential ingredient for success in life. To me, this means being kind to others and offering supportive feedback on their actions and words. By staying positive, we demonstrate our maturity and act as excellent role models for the people we live and work with every day.

He explained that he felt bad because his friend had studied just as hard but did not receive any candy.

To conclude, having a positive outlook is the ultimate key to success. Whenever we feel overwhelmed by negative energy, we should try to understand that the situation could be much worse. Ultimately, a positive mindset allows us to gain far more in life than we would if we kept a negative attitude.

Would you want to add two extra hours to your school schedule just to have a four-day week? Personally, I do not think this is a good idea. Students need time for their families, other responsibilities, and simply to enjoy their youth instead of being stuck in a classroom for ten hours a day.

One major reason to oppose this change is that many students value time with their families. Some relatives might live far away, and students need the flexibility to visit them whenever possible. Additionally, some teenagers want to spend more time helping their elderly grandparents who might struggle with daily tasks. Spending time with cousins and other relatives is also important, especially if they have not seen each other for a long time. These family connections are vital, and a ten-hour school day would make them much harder to maintain.

Furthermore, many students have busy schedules and responsibilities after school. For instance, athletes need to attend sports practices as soon as the school day ends. If school lasted ten hours, they would not have enough time for their training. Other students have serious duties at home, such as babysitting younger siblings while their parents are at work. Some students even have part-time jobs and could get into trouble with their employers if they cannot arrive on time. Forcing everyone to stay at school all day ignores these essential commitments.

It is also important for young people to have enough free time. Instead of studying or working all day, students should be able to go shopping or hang out with their friends. This leisure time allows them to relax and spend quality moments with their parents. We are only young once, and we should be able to enjoy our lives before we enter the adult world of full-time employment.

Finally, longer days would likely lead to extreme exhaustion. Many students are already tired of the heavy workload, and adding more hours might cause them to give up on their studies entirely. For example, when I finish school, I usually have to go home immediately to take care of my little sister because my mother is busy. If I stayed at school for ten hours and then had to help at home, I would be too exhausted to do any homework. I would probably just fall asleep as soon as I got back.

In conclusion, extending the school day to ten hours is not a practical solution. it takes away from family time, interferes with personal responsibilities, and leads to burnout. Students need a balance between education and their personal lives to stay motivated.

Many people believe that online education is a great choice for learners. It can improve attendance, reduce social issues, and support students with health conditions or disabilities. While some critics argue that staying home leads to laziness, distance learning offers significant advantages for both students and educational institutions.

One major benefit of remote learning is improved attendance. When students can study from home, they are much more likely to participate in their classes regularly. A common struggle for many is waking up very early to prepare for a long school day. These early starts often leave students feeling exhausted and unmotivated, whereas learning from home allows for a more manageable schedule that keeps them engaged.

Furthermore, distance learning is essential for students with physical disabilities or chronic illnesses that prevent them from attending a traditional campus. Every child deserves an education, and online platforms ensure that these students are not left behind. Providing equal opportunities for those with health challenges is perhaps the most significant reason to support this model of schooling.

Another advantage is the reduction of social conflict. In traditional schools, many students face bullying or unnecessary social drama, which can distract them from their studies. By learning at home, students can focus entirely on their academics in a safe environment. Consequently, schools will see a decrease in behavioral issues and harassment.

Opponents might claim that distance learning makes students irresponsible or lazy. However, students should have the freedom to choose the environment that suits them best. If a student lacks motivation, that is a personal issue rather than a fault of the system itself. In fact, many believe that managing one's own schedule online actually builds greater responsibility and discipline.

Parents should support their children in making this choice. The only major difference is that they are not physically in a classroom. While not all peers are difficult to be around, the environment can still be challenging. Personally, if I had the chance to use video conferencing for my education, I would definitely take it.

Research suggests that students who decide on a career before high school may find more success later in life. However, this early commitment often leads to extreme pressure. Choosing a career path at such a young age is a mental burden that should be avoided. It causes excessive stress, forces students to focus on a distant future rather than their current development, and ignores the fact that high school is a time when people naturally change their minds.

The first reason why students should not commit to a career early is the increased stress it brings to the high school experience. While having a plan might seem like a good idea, it often makes school much harder. When you are locked into one path, you feel a constant need to achieve goals faster than everyone else. This creates a situation where it is difficult to focus on other classes because your mind is preoccupied with a single objective. High school is supposed to be a place where education transforms you, and being too focused on one goal prevents that growth.

Additionally, the pressure involved in these early decisions can be overwhelming. Many students feel they must stick to a specific path to make their parents, teachers, or school administrators proud. As the weeks and months go by, this pressure continues to build. Eventually, this can lead to feelings of sadness or even depression because the student is no longer pursuing a goal for themselves, but rather to satisfy the expectations of others.

Furthermore, high school is a time of discovery. It is very different from middle school and is rarely like the movies. It is a place where students encounter many new elective subjects. It is illogical to commit to a career before you have even had the chance to try these different classes. You might discover a passion you never knew you had if you remain open to new experiences.

In my opinion, it is better to explore various interests rather than committing too soon. Experience shows that it is better to take classes you enjoy and see where they lead. Real life is often quite different from what is portrayed on television. Everyone is unique, and a career is just one aspect of who you are. You should not push yourself to make such a permanent choice while you are still so young.

Deciding on a professional path while still in high school is an excellent way for students to prepare for their adult lives. In certain societies, young people are expected to choose a career before they even graduate. Making this commitment at an early age is a very beneficial strategy for several reasons.

One major advantage is that it allows students to reach their objectives much sooner. For instance, if a student begins focusing on subjects related to a specific job during high school, they can often finish their university degree faster. Because they have already gained foundational knowledge from their school courses, they might only need a year or two of college instead of the traditional four years.

Furthermore, choosing a career early helps students develop a more mature and responsible attitude toward their future. Taking specialized courses can increase their motivation to succeed and help them realize that they are in charge of their own progress. It teaches them that having a solid career is the key to a successful life, which can change their perspective on the importance of education.

On the other hand, some critics argue that this approach puts too much pressure on teenagers. They believe that worrying about a specific career and taking extra classes can lead to physical and mental exhaustion. Consequently, these people think it is better to wait until college to make such a significant decision.

However, delaying this choice until university can be problematic. Students who wait often feel rushed and may pick a subject they are not truly passionate about. This frequently results in spending extra years in school or even dropping out entirely, which can negatively impact their future job opportunities.

To conclude, committing to a career at a young age is a wise decision. It helps students prepare for the future and reach their goals more efficiently. By knowing what to expect before they reach college, they can avoid many common struggles and set themselves up for a successful life.

Education plays a vital role in preparing individuals for a rapidly changing world. It shapes how future professionals approach problems and has historically empowered generations to achieve great things, from space exploration to solving global crises. However, despite the importance of schooling, I believe that school boards should not extend the daily schedule. The current seven-hour day is already sufficient for academic and personal growth, and adding more time would likely lead to increased stress, unproductivity, and significant scheduling conflicts for families and staff.

To begin with, the existing seven-hour schedule is already a demanding process. From the moment students arrive—sometimes dealing with transportation issues or early arrivals—their day is packed with mental and physical challenges. They must navigate complex academic concepts while simultaneously managing their social lives and personal responsibilities, such as organizing their lockers or planning group projects with friends. This timeframe is already filled with high-pressure situations that can be quite exhausting for the average student.

Extending the school day would likely amplify these difficulties. A longer day often means a heavier workload, including more assignments and a potential increase in homework. When students are forced to focus on specific subjects for too long, they may become bored or lose interest, making the extra time unproductive. Instead of helping, an extension could make the school day feel overwhelming and impossible to manage, leading to a negative attitude toward learning.

Another major concern is the impact on the schedules of students, parents, and faculty. Many students are involved in extracurricular activities like baseball or swimming, which require adequate time after school to function properly. If the school day is lengthened, these activities may suffer. Furthermore, parents and guardians often have strict work schedules; a change in school hours could make it difficult for them to coordinate transportation or spend quality time with their children. Faculty members would also be burdened, as they would need to stay even later to complete their professional duties and prepare their classrooms.

While there are some potential benefits to a longer day, such as more time for socialization or the opportunity to finish homework at school, these do not outweigh the negatives. Even if students have more time to study, the quality of their work may decline due to fatigue. Unproductive elements will always exist, and simply adding more hours to the clock does not guarantee better results.

In summary, I am against the prolongation of the school day because of the stress it places on students and the logistical problems it creates for families. The current seven-hour schedule is already full of meaningful activities and learning opportunities. We should carefully consider the irreversible impact that such a change could have on the well-being of the entire school community.

As a student-athlete who plays both soccer and football, I strongly agree with the philosopher Ralph Waldo Emerson’s idea that we must attempt things past our mastery if we want to grow.

I have to work harder than before and develop new levels of talent to earn a starting spot on the team.

Furthermore, this mindset leads to long-term success in life. For example, the founder of Amazon started his business in a small garage. He would never have built a global empire if he had stayed comfortable in that garage instead of taking bigger risks. Similarly, even though Donald Trump already had wealth and fame, he chose to push himself further by competing for the presidency. We can also see this with the iPhone; the company continues to upgrade the technology to attract more users. Many successful entrepreneurs take the "bigger step" of getting a loan to expand their business, showing that growth requires moving past what is familiar.

Some people might argue that you only need to try new things rather than exceeding what you have already mastered. However, simply adding variety does not always lead to real progress. For instance, adding a different type of exercise to a workout won't make me stronger if the weight remains the same. Likewise, a business cannot truly expand if it stays in a garage forever. To achieve real growth and gain more customers, a person must take the risk of moving to a larger space or seeking financial investment.

In conclusion, I agree with Emerson because staying where you are comfortable leads to stagnation. Even if you are already excellent at what you do, you must strive to accomplish things that are currently beyond your reach. This is the only way to ensure continuous growth and lasting success in any field.

Most students enjoy summer vacation, but some educators think that summer break is too long and students do not retain information as easily as they would in the fall. Because of this a lot of educators think we should have year- round school years. This would be shorter breaks in the summer (3-4 weeks) and longer more spread-out breaks throughout the year. I disagree with this statement and believe that summer break should stay the way it is.

The first reason I disagree with this statement is that it would ruin certain summer activities or even business plans. Think about all the activities in the summer that kids usually take part in, this could be sports, some sort of trip, etc. All of these activities students would preferably do during summer break. They have this preference because they see the summer as a perfect time to do all these activities without having to balance their education as well. They can put most of their time on this activity. The same preference applies to things like summer jobs or internships. During the summer they can learn important values like how to save and earn money. Or if a certain student has a chosen career path they can explore this career path by going in a internship for that spesicifc job. For all of these activities students at the very least would be discouraged to participate in if there was a year-round school year.

The second and probably most important reason is pertaining to the students mental health. An article, by Complex News writing about kids mental health stated, that over 40% of kids by the end of their freshmen year in high school are depressed or overall feel exhausted and depleted mentally. The article continues to say that this number from the time of their freshmen year only increases after each school year. Students use the summer break as a way for their brain to refresh from the long almost ten month school year. Students need this time to relax their brain and get ready for the next year of education. As a student, I can say that during school my brain goes into this state where I am mostly just focused on school work. And I can admit that my brain at multiple points during the year is worn down and damaged by always be in this state. My brain does not get a chance to heal from this until the summer, when school is over. So if we were to hypothetically have a year-round school year, this would mean that the brain would also be in this damaged state year round. If this were the case than the brain of the student would eventually just break and shut down. No student should have to experience that because of a year- round school year.

Although the strongest reason for this year-round school year is that students cannot properly retain enough information for the next school year, I think I have a much stronger counter claim and solution to this problem. A very simple way to take care of the problem of retaining information, is to make mandatory (but simple) assignments from the previous year for the student to complete so that they don't forget this information. This way students can have their long summer break to refresh their brain and do their activities, without them having to forget any information. You get the best of both worlds with no need for a year-round school year.

In conclusion I think my assertions for the summer break to stay the way it is is much stronger than year-round school year argument. Having a year-round school year would be unnecessarily tedious and dangerous as it would negatively affect summer activities and mental health. As someone said once upon a time "Don't fix it if it ain't broke."
